story.title: You arrive at the walking street full of food.
story.text: The evening market is busy, and Alex sees many local dishes at small food stalls.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Wow! Everything smells so good. I want to say this naturally.

choices.text: I would like to try some local street food.

feedback.reaction: Good sentence 👍 It is polite and natural.

choices.text: I would like try some street local food.

feedback.reaction: Wrong structure ❌ The phrase needs 'to try' and a natural adjective order.

choices.text: Some local food street I like would try.

feedback.reaction: Not correct 😅 The word order is confusing.

story.title: Alex tries spicy food.
story.text: Alex takes a small bite and realizes the dish is stronger than expected.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Oh! This is spicy. I want to explain that it surprised me.

choices.text: This dish is much spicier than I expected.

feedback.reaction: Correct! 🌶️ The comparison is clear and natural.

choices.text: This dish is more spicy than me expected.

feedback.reaction: Wrong grammar ❌ Use 'spicier than I expected'.

choices.text: This dish much spicy than expected I.

feedback.reaction: Incorrect 😅 The sentence order is not natural.

story.title: Alex enjoys dessert.
story.text: Alex tries a cold dessert after the spicy food and wants to describe the taste more precisely.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: This dessert is sweet, but it also feels cool and light.

choices.text: The dessert is both sweet and refreshing.

feedback.reaction: Nice description 🍰 The sentence combines two qualities clearly.

choices.text: The dessert both is sweet and refreshing.

feedback.reaction: Wrong order ❌ Place 'both' before the first adjective phrase.

choices.text: Refreshing and sweet dessert is both the.

feedback.reaction: Incorrect 😅 The word order is not grammatical.

story.title: Alex asks for your opinion.
story.text: Alex wants to know whether you like the food and why it tastes good.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Do you like this food? Why?

choices.text: Yes, I like it, especially because the flavors are balanced.

feedback.reaction: Great answer 👍 It gives an opinion and a reason.

choices.text: Yes, I like because balanced the flavors are.

feedback.reaction: Wrong structure ❌ The reason clause needs natural word order.

choices.text: I yes like it very because flavors.

feedback.reaction: Incorrect 😅 The sentence is missing a clear structure.

story.title: The night is ending and Alex reflects.
story.text: The walking street is closing soon. Alex enjoyed the food, the people, and the local atmosphere.

choices.text: I'm glad you enjoyed it; walking streets are a great way to experience local culture.

feedback.reaction: Perfect ending 😊 The response is warm and meaningful.

choices.text: I am glad enjoyed you it because culture local experience.

feedback.reaction: Wrong sentence ❌ The word order makes the meaning unclear.

choices.text: I do not care, but the walking street is a local culture experience way.
